title: 4 day full body split
author: Jack S.
desc: A 4 day split with an emphasis on progressive overload and the use of compound, accessory, and body weight movements.

ex.note: Warm up to two top sets for a weight that you know would be difficult to hit for 12 clean reps. This can be as many sets as you need to prepare yourself for two max effort sets.

1st set- weight is just right for a solid set of 10
2nd set- top set. Will be focus for progressive overload. RPE 10
3rd set- back off set, focus on form and control. Try to get all 10 reps. RPE 10
Again, take as many warmup sets as you need to reach a weight that will be challenging for a solid set of 12. The 2nd set will be your focus for progressive overload, try to hit as much weight for 8.

Reps are 16 total. So 8 forward and 8 back. Or however many it takes to lunge the whole turf. But shoot for 16 total reps at least. 
Can swap with Bulgarian split squats
Calves are a small muscle group, so they benefit from less time in between sets. Try and shoot for no longer than 90 second in between sets.
Warmup sets until you reach a weight that is difficult to hit for 8 reps. Do not add weight until you can hit 8 reps per set at your current weight.
Try to get at least 10 for the first two sets, then really try to add some weight for the last two. It’s okay to fail at 8 reps.
Similar to bench, warm up to these two top sets. Do not add weight until you can comfortably use your current weight for two full sets of 12.
Focus on the stretch and add in some Kelso shrugs once you can no longer complete a full rep. Think of these as shrugs for your traps.
Higher volume today. It’s ok to use less weight because you really just want to reach the 10 reps per set.

Aim for heavier weight in the second set. Try to add weight to this set each week for progressive overload. The 3rd should be a back off set emphasizing control and reaching at least 8 reps. 
B. Smith
Don’t be afraid to go light, it’s most important to emphasize the burn on these.
Try to go heavier every couple weeks, but don’t go up in weight until you can hit 10 reps per set with a pause at the bottom of each repetition.
Do these seated, don’t be afraid to start swinging the weight once you get tired to get more reps.
Try to go really heavy on these for at least 8 reps.
